lens: Code quality — readability, maintainability, error handling, test coverage, deletion-safety
answer: Reviewed at merge commit 70b83631 (not working tree, which is a sibling branch behind PR12). PR is a clean path-string consolidation: git mv preserves history, all 7 inbound refs across 5 files rewritten consistently, ADR-0117 documents both actions clearly with naming justification and consequences. Rust kernel + app + tests all reference infra/kyverno/oya-vcs-admission consistently (kernel lib.rs lines 83, 247, 321 + app main.rs line 38 ARGO_MANIFEST constant + kernel test fixture). All 4 rewritten JSONs (application.json + 3 evidence JSONs) parse cleanly via jq empty. .gitignore append (.audit/) is correct and matches the actual change (only .audit/ added — .config/ correctly NOT ignored because CI requires .config/nextest.toml [profile.ci]; ADR-0117 documents this rationale). One residual reference to 'deploy/gitops/oya-vcs-admission' remains inside ADR-0117 itself, which is acceptable historical context (before/after narrative). No production source/config file has a leftover ref. Test coverage existed prior — the change only modifies path-string constants; tests rerun with new paths (kernel passing_manifest fixture + app argo_manifest_path test both rewritten consistently). Maintainability improves (one admission-policy root). Deletion-safety good (history-preserving git mv). Hyperscaler bar: a Stripe/Palantir engineer would accept this — small scope, full citation, ADR, consistent rewrites, no dead code, no compat seam. Minor F5 nits below.
key_claims: All 4 manifest/evidence JSONs at merge commit parse via jq empty
Zero leftover deploy/gitops/oya-vcs-admission refs in production source/config/evidence at the merge commit (the 1 ADR mention is historical context)
Rust path-string rewrites are consistent across kernel lib.rs (3 sites), app main.rs (1 site), and kernel test fixture (1 site)

ADR-0117 PR-body Task 1 says .config/ was added to .gitignore; the actual merge only added .audit/ — ADR body correctly explains why .config/nextest.toml stays tracked; the PR description summary is stale relative to the merged content
Naming justification present (infra/kyverno already established admission-policy root; no new name introduced)
Deletion-safety: history-preserving git mv detected by git (rename in stat output)

anti_patterns_detected: Stale PR description: body says .config/ was gitignored but merge does not include that (.gitignore append is only .audit/). The ADR corrects this. Low impact for merged PR; readers comparing PR body to commit may be confused.

Magic path string repeated across 5+ sites instead of a single const/helper — pre-existing condition, not introduced by this PR, but the rewrite exposed how brittle path-strings-as-config is; a single ARGO_MANIFEST_PATH const at kernel level would have made this PR a 1-line change

findings.summary: PR description Task 1 claims .config/ was gitignored and untracked; actual merge only ignored .audit/. ADR-0117 has the correct story but the PR body is stale.
findings.recommended_action: Post a follow-up PR comment or amend release notes to clarify .config/nextest.toml stays tracked; align future PR body to merged content before squash-merge.

findings.recommended_action: Extract a single pub const ARGO_APPLICATION_MANIFEST_PATH in oya-vcs-provider-execution-gate-kernel and have both the kernel sites and the app binary import it. Defer to a separate refactor PR.
